title: refactor(ci): consolidate lint/test/release workflows, upgrade actions, optimize cache parallelism
author: Aisha Khan
description: Motivation: Our CI repo has grown a number of separate workflow files (lint, tests, release, and per-language matrices) that duplicate setup logic and make caching and parallelism hard to tune. This PR consolidates the major workflows into three opinionated pipelines (lint, test, release) with shared reusable steps, upgrades several GH Actions to the latest stable versions, and introduces a light-weight cache-parallelism helper to reduce CI timeouts and cache contention. Goals: 1) reduce duplicated workflow YAML and maintenance surface; 2) improve cache hit rates across matrix jobs; 3) reduce overall CI runtime by optimizing parallelism; 4) keep release automation behavior identical and auditable. Changes include: - Consolidated .github/workflows/{lint.yml,test.yml,release.yml} into a shared pattern using reusable workflows and composite actions. - Bumped actions/checkout@v3 -> actions/checkout@v4 where safe, setup-node@v3 -> setup-node@v4, actions/cache hygiene bumps. - Added tools/ci/cache-utils.sh to compute per-job cache keys and a small helper to coordinate parallel cache writes. - Introduced a shared .github/workflows/templates/common-setup.yml reusable workflow used by lint/test/release to centralize node/toolkit setup and secrets handling. - Tightened job timeouts and added explicit retries on flakey network steps. See linked Linear items and notes below. Checklist: - [x] Consolidate shared setup into reusable workflow (common-setup.yml) - [x] Replace duplicate matrix definitions with a single matrix template - [x] Bump GH Actions where compatibility validated - [x] Add cache-parallelism helper and docs - [x] Run CI across monorepo and validate builds on redwood, sdk repos - [x] Update README/CONTRIBUTING to reference new workflow layout Notes: - Release workflow behavior preserved: the release job still requires the same set of checks and release automation secrets. We validated a dry-run on the staging repo and performed a canary release in the dev org. - We intentionally left out a single legacy workflow used by the private-installer repo; that will be migrated in a follow-up (ENG-2432). Links: Linear ENG-2314 (CI consolidation), ENG-2401 (cache parallelism); PRs referenced during testing: #104503, #104500. If any team needs special matrix configurations (e.g., older Node versions), add an override in .github/workflows/overrides/. This description is intentionally concise; details are in the commit list and changed files section.
commits: chore(ci): add reusable common-setup.yml and composite action for node/tool setup
feat(ci): consolidate lint workflow into reusable template + matrix simplification
feat(ci): consolidate test workflow and introduce cache-utils.sh for parallel writes
chore(deps): bump actions/checkout@v3 -> @v4, setup-node@v3 -> @v4, fix breaking inputs
fix(ci): adjust timeouts and add retry for flaky network downloads
docs(ci): update CONTRIBUTING.md and dev docs for new workflow layout
review_comments: Liam O'Connor: Can we avoid a hard bump to actions/checkout@v4 in the release workflow? We saw a permissions change last quarter that affected tags. Aisha: Verfied v4 preserves tag behavior for our use; added explicit persist-credentials: true on the release job to be safe.

Maria Vasquez: The cache helper seems useful but introduces another bash script to maintain. Can we document failure modes? Aisha: Added comments to tools/ci/cache-utils.sh and a short section in CONTRIBUTING.md describing when to fallback to single-writer cache behavior.

Devon Chen: CI runtime on large matrix still spikes occasionally. Suggest we cap parallelism per runner group. Aisha: Added a per-matrix concurrency control and job-level timeout increases; noted follow-up to add runner-group aware throttling (ENG-2455).
QA: Observed flaky integration test during canary run; reran pipeline and it passed. Added a retry wrapper around the infra provisioning step.
release_notes:
- Consolidated CI workflows to reduce duplication and improve maintenance
- Bumped several GH Actions to latest stable releases
- Introduced cache-parallelism helper to improve cache hit rates and reduce CI timeouts
- No user-facing changes; internal developer experience (CI speed and reliability) improved
